question: What constitutes the construction sector in Uganda and how are construction companies and professionals regulated?
answer: The construction sector in Uganda encompasses the planning, design, financing, erection, repair, renovation, and maintenance of civil infrastructure (roads, bridges, railways, dams), residential structures, commercial complexes, and industrial facilities. The sector is regulated across several statutory and professional bodies: 1) Construction Companies — registered with URSB (Certificate of Incorporation/Form 20), licensed by KCCA/Local Councils, registered with the Uganda National Association of Building and Civil Engineering Contractors (UNABCEC), and certified with NEMA environmental approvals; 2) Construction Professionals — licensed by statutory boards including the Engineers Registration Board (ERB), Architects Registration Board (ARB), and Surveyors Registration Board (SRB); 3) Tax Registration — URA Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) required for all procurement bidding, building permits, and public works contracts.

question: What income taxes apply to construction companies and consulting construction professionals in Uganda?
answer: 1) Construction Companies: Taxed at a standard thirty percent (30%) Corporation Income Tax (CIT) on net chargeable profits (gross turnover less allowable expenses including raw materials, plant hire, fuel, casual wages, equipment repairs, and subcontract charges). Provisional returns are filed twice yearly (by end of 6th month and end of 12th month) via Form DT-1001; 2) Sole Proprietor Professionals: Professional consulting fees (architectural, engineering, surveying) earned by individuals are taxed under graduated resident individual income tax rates up to 40% (top bracket above UGX 10M monthly); professional service providers cannot pay presumptive turnover tax and must file formal income tax returns; 3) PAYE: Mandatory monthly withholding and remittance for all salaried and site-based permanent personnel.

question: How does Withholding Tax (WHT) apply to construction contracts, subcontracting, and professional consulting fees?
answer: Under Section 119, 120, and 86 of the Income Tax Act: 1) Supply of Construction Works & Materials: Designated withholding agents (government entities, MDAs, and gazetted corporate entities) must withhold 6% WHT on payments for construction contracts and building material supplies exceeding UGX 1,000,000; 2) Professional Consulting Fees: 6% WHT applies to payments made to resident engineers, architects, project managers, and quantity surveyors; 3) Non-Resident Contractors & Engineers: 15% WHT is withheld on payments made to foreign non-resident engineering or construction consultants (or 10% on subcontractors for mining and petroleum operations); 4) 6% WHT Exemption: Compliant construction firms with clean tax filing and payment records over the preceding 3 years can apply for and receive a 12-month renewable WHT Exemption Certificate under Section 119(5)(f) ITA.

question: What VAT rules, EFRIS invoicing requirements, and deemed VAT provisions apply to construction projects in Uganda?
answer: 1) Standard Rate: Construction contracts, civil works, project management, and building material sales attract 18% VAT; 2) Mandatory EFRIS: All VAT-registered construction companies and suppliers must issue e-invoices/e-receipts bearing a 20-digit Fiscal Document Number (FDN); developers and main contractors cannot claim input tax credit without valid EFRIS invoices; 3) Deemed VAT for Aid-Funded Projects: Under Section 24(5) of the VAT Act, VAT charged by suppliers or subcontractors to a contractor executing an official donor or aid-funded project is deemed paid, provided the goods and services are for direct and exclusive use on the aid-funded project; 4) Specialized Hospital Development Exemption: Feasibility studies, architectural design, construction services, locally produced materials, and machinery for developers investing at least USD 5 million to build a specialized referral hospital are 100% VAT exempt.

question: What customs duty exemptions and capital allowances are available for construction plant, machinery, and surveying gear?
answer: Under the EAC Common External Tariff (CET), EACCMA, and Income Tax Act: 1) Heavy Cranes for Construction: 0% import duty by tariff, and VAT is deferrable for VAT-registered construction firms; 2) Surveying Equipment: GPS devices, theodolites, optical line-of-sight levels, and electronic rangefinders enjoy 0% import duty by tariff (VAT payable); 3) Tippers & Dump Trucks: Heavy dump trucks exceeding 20 tonnes gross vehicle weight (GVW) enjoy 0% import duty for one year (5 to 20 tonnes GVW attract reduced 10% duty); 4) Scaffolding: 100% exempt from import duty when sourced from within the East African Community (EAC); 5) Temporary Machinery Imports: Specialized heavy earthmoving machinery imported temporarily enjoys tax suspension under customs security bond, cancelled upon re-export; 6) Industrial Building Allowance: 20% initial capital deduction for industrial buildings outside Kampala (50 km radius) plus 5% annual straight-line depreciation over 20 years.
